extracted.intended_audience: FCC licensees, applicants, and their attorneys/filers (wireless, media, international, and other communications services)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules and standards governing FCC authorizations, discontinuance and termination of service, computation methods, settlement procedures, application/fee schedules, and payment procedures for various communications services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-specific performance requirements for partitioning/disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to geographic partitioning, spectrum disaggregation, or a combination of both, have two options to satisfy service-specific performance requirements (i.e., construction and operation requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option 1: Each party may certify that it will individually satisfy any service-specific requirements and, upon failure, must individually face any service-specific performance penalties. Option 2: Both parties may agree to share responsibility for any service-specific requirements; upon failure to meet their shared service-specific performance requirements, both parties will be subject to any service-specific penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unjust enrichment for transfers to ineligible entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees making installment payments or that received a bidding credit, that partition their licenses or disaggregate their spectrum to entities that do not meet the eligibility standards for installment payments or bidding credits, are subject to the unjust enrichment requirements of § 1.2111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers or partitions to ineligible entities may trigger unjust enrichment obligations under §1.2111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to respond to official communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees or applicants in the Wireless Radio Services receiving official notice of an apparent or actual violation of a federal statute, international agreement, Executive Order, or regulation pertaining to communications shall respond in writing within 10 days to the office of the FCC originating the notice, unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be complete and self-contained without reference to other communications unless copies of such other communications are attached. Licensees or applicants may respond via ULS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic termination on permanent discontinuance
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee's authorization will automatically terminate, without specific Commission action, if the licensee permanently discontinues service or operations under the license during the license term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensee is subject to this provision commencing on the date it is required to be providing service or operating (see § 1.953(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 180-day Rule for Geographic Licenses (permanent discontinuance definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent discontinuance of service or operations for Covered Geographic Licenses is defined as 180 consecutive days during which a licensee does not operate or, for commercial mobile radio service providers, does not provide service to at least one subscriber that is not affiliated with, controlled by, or related to the licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 180-day threshold is reached the license is considered permanently discontinued and subject to automatic termination under §1.953(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: 365-day Rule for Site-based Licenses (permanent discontinuance definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent discontinuance of service or operations for Covered Site-based Licenses is defined as 365 consecutive days during which a licensee does not operate or, for commercial mobile radio service providers, does not provide service to at least one subscriber that is not affiliated with, controlled by, or related to the providing carrier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 365-day threshold is reached the license is considered permanently discontinued and subject to automatic termination under §1.953(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: 365-day Rule for public safety licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent discontinuance of operations is defined as 365 consecutive days during which a licensee does not operate. This 365-day rule applies to public safety licenses issued based on eligibility under § 90.20 or § 90.529 or licenses issued in conjunction with a waiver pursuant to section 337 of the Communications Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public safety authorizations that do not operate for 365 consecutive days are considered permanently discontinued under §1.953(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel keepers do not constitute operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Operation of channel keepers (devices that transmit test signals, tones, color bars, or some combination of these, for example) does not constitute operation or service for the purposes of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of channel keepers cannot be used to show compliance with operation/service requirements under §1.953(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements upon permanent discontinuance
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that permanently discontinues service as defined in this section must notify the Commission of the discontinuance within 10 days by filing FCC Form 601 or 605 requesting license cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authorization will automatically terminate if service or operations are permanently discontinued as defined in this section, even if a licensee fails to file the required form requesting license cancellation. (See §1.953(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension request for discontinuance periods
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee may file a request for a longer discontinuance period for good cause. An extension request must be filed at least 30 days before the end of the applicable 180-day or 365-day discontinuance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing of an extension request will automatically extend the discontinuance period a minimum of the later of an additional 30 days or the date upon which the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau acts on the request (§1.953(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizations remain valid until termination under rules; Commission revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations in general remain valid until terminated in accordance with this section, except that the Commission may revoke an authorization pursuant to section 312 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 47 U.S.C. 312 and related subsections for revocation authority (intro to §1.955).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration of authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations automatically terminate, without specific Commission action, on the expiration date specified therein, unless a timely application for renewal is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No authorization granted under the provisions of this part shall be for a term longer than ten years, except to the extent a longer term is authorized under §27.13 of part 27 of this chapter (§1.955(a)(1)). See also §1.949 on renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic termination for failure to meet construction or coverage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations automatically terminate (in whole or in part as set forth in the service rules), without specific Commission action, if the licensee fails to meet applicable construction or coverage requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.946(c) for construction/coverage requirement details (§1.955(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: STA automatic termination and extension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Special temporary authority (STA) automatically terminates without specific Commission action upon failure to comply with the terms and conditions therein, or at the end of the period specified therein, unless a timely request for an extension of the STA term is filed in accordance with §1.931 of this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a timely filed request for extension of the STA term is dismissed or denied, the STA automatically terminates, without specific Commission action, on the day after the applicant or the applicant's attorney is notified of the Commission's action dismissing or denying the request for extension (§1.955(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination on submission for cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations submitted by licensees for cancellation terminate when the Commission gives Public Notice of such action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement conferences: purposes and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are encouraged to use alternative dispute resolution procedures to settle disputes. In any contested proceeding, the Commission may direct the parties or their attorneys to appear before it for a conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposes of conferences include: (1) obtain admissions of fact or stipulations; (2) consider amendments to pleadings or additional submissions; (3) consider simplification or narrowing of issues; (4) encourage settlement by agreement; (5) consider other matters aiding resolution. Conferences may be scheduled in person or by telephone; failure to appear after reasonable notice will be deemed a failure to prosecute, subjecting the party's application or petition to dismissal (§1.956(a)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for amateur radio operator license examinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each candidate for an amateur radio license which requires the applicant to pass one or more examination elements must present the Volunteer Examiners (VEs) with a properly completed FCC Form 605 prior to the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon completion VEs will grade tests; successful applicants have application forwarded to a Volunteer-Examiner Coordinator (VEC); VEs issue a certificate for successful completion and the VEC forwards the application to the Commission's Gettysburg facility (§1.957).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required method for distance computation
rubrics_metrics.description: The method given in this section must be used to compute the distance between any two locations, except that, for computation of distance involving stations in Canada and Mexico, methods for distance computation specified in the applicable international agreement, if any, must be used instead. The result must be rounded to the nearest tenth of a kilometer. The method is sufficiently accurate for distances not exceeding 475 km (295 miles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include: (a) convert lat/long from DMS to degree-decimal; (b) calculate mean geodetic latitude (ML) by averaging the two latitudes; (c) compute KPD_lat = 111.13209 − 0.56605 cos 2ML + 0.00120 cos 4ML; (d) compute KPD_lon = 111.41513 cos ML − 0.09455 cos 3ML + 0.00012 cos 5ML; (e) NS = KPD_lat × (LAT1dd − LAT2dd); (f) EW = KPD_lon × (LON1dd − LON2dd); (g) DIST = sqrt(NS^2 + EW^2); (h) defined terms include LAT1dd/LON1dd, ML, KPD_lat, KPD_lon, NS, EW, DIST (§1.958(a)-(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of average terrain elevation
rubrics_metrics.description: Average terrain elevation must be calculated by computer using elevations from a 30 second point or better topographic data file, except as otherwise specified. The file must be identified. If a 30 second point data file is used, the elevation data must be processed for intermediate points using interpolation techniques; otherwise, the nearest point may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radial average terrain elevation: average elevation along a straight line path from 3 to 16 km radially from antenna site; exclude portions over foreign territory or water unless radial again passes over U.S. land between 16 and 134 km away. Use at least 50 evenly spaced data points per radial. Average terrain elevation is the average of the eight cardinal radials. For locations in Dade and Broward Counties, Florida, may assume average terrain elevation of 3 meters (§1.959(a)-(c)). Manual determinations allowed in disputes if results differ significantly from computer-derived averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose and collect statutory charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to impose and collect these charges is contained in section 8 of the Communications Act, as amended by sections 102 and 103 of title I of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2018, 47 U.S.C. 158, which directs the Commission to assess and collect application fees to recover the costs of the Commission to process applications (§1.1101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the statutory basis for the schedules and procedures in Subpart G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges: general instructions for wireless telecommunications services
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the wireless application fees in this section have a regulatory fee component that must be paid at the time of a new or a renewal of a wireless application. In tables, amounts in the 'Fee Amount' column are for application fees only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Wireless Filing Guide for payment type codes and associated regulatory fees. Application fee payments are required to be made electronically using the Commission's Registration System (CORES) once an application has been submitted in the ULS. CORES links and Wireless Filing Guide URLs provided (§1.1102(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and fee schedule for site-based licensed services (Table 1 to §1.1102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Site-based licensed services are services for which an applicant's initial application generally provides the exact technical parameters of planned operations (transmitter location, area of operation, frequency, power). Examples include land mobile systems, point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, radiolocation and radionavigation systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists fees for 'New license, major modification' ($105), 'Extension Requests' ($50), 'Special temporary authority' ($150), 'Assignment/transfer of control, initial call sign' ($50), subsequent call signs $35 (capped at 10), rule waivers $425, renewal $35, spectrum leasing $35, and other listed items. See §1.1102(b) and Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and fee schedule for personal license applications (Table 2 to §1.1102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal licenses authorize shared use of certain spectrum bands or provide required permits and focus only on eligibility, not technical review. Examples: Amateur Radio, Ship, Aircraft, Commercial Radio Operator, GMRS, Vanity, Restricted Operator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists fees including 'New license, modification' $35, 'Special temporary authority' $35, 'Rule waiver' $35, 'Renewal' $35, 'Vanity Call Sign' $35, and references Wireless Telecommunications Bureau Fee Filing Guide for some services (§1.1102(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and fee schedule for geographic-based licenses (Table 3 to §1.1102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic-based licenses authorize construction anywhere within a geographic area's boundary and generally do not require prior Commission approval of specific transmitter locations. Examples include 220-222 MHz, Upper Microwave Flexible Use, 600 MHz, 700 MHz Lower Band services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table lists fees including 'New License (other than Auctioned Licenses), Major Modification' $360, 'New License (Auctioned Licenses... )' $3,730, 'Renewal' $50, 'Minor Modification' $225, 'Construction Notification/Extensions' $325, 'STA' $375, 'Assignment/Transfer initial call sign' $230, subsequent call sign $35, 'Spectrum Leasing' $185, and rule waivers $425, etc. See §1.1102(d) and Table 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges for equipment approval and experimental radio services (§1.1103 Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists payment type codes and fee amounts for equipment and experimental service applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Assignment of Grantee Code (EAG) $35.00; New Station Authorization (EAE) $140.00; Modification of Authorization (EAE) $140.00; Renewal (EAE) $140.00; Confidentiality Request (EAD) $50. See §1.1103 Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges for media services (§1.1104 multi-table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets application fee amounts by media service type (full power TV, commercial AM/FM, FM translators, TV translators/LPTV, cable television, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides many specific fees (examples): Full power TV new construction permit $5,000 (no auction) or $5,675 (if auction); Commercial AM new/major change $4,675 (or $5,350 if auction); Commercial FM new/major change $3,870 (or $4,545 if auction); FM translators new $830 (no auction) or $1,505 (if auction). Also includes fees for renewals, assignments, transfers, special temporary authority, petitions, biennial reports, foreign ownership petitions (Table 5 $2,920), cable TV fees, and others. See §1.1104 Tables 1–7 for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges for wireline competition services (Table 1 to §1.1105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists fee amounts and payment type codes for wireline competition service filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Domestic 214 Transfers of Control (CDU) $1,445; Domestic 214 STA (CDV) $755; VoIP Numbering (CDY) $1,560; Standard Tariff Filing (CQK) $1,040; Complex Tariff Filing (CQL/CQM) $7,680/$3,840. See §1.1105 Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges for enforcement services (Table 1 to §1.1106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists fee amounts for enforcement-related filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Formal Complaint (CIZ) $605; Pole Attachment Complaint (TPC) $605; Petitions Regarding Law Enforcement Assistance Capability under CALEA (CLEA) $8,155. See §1.1106 Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges for international services (§1.1107 multi-table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed fee schedules for international filings including cable landing licenses, international Section 214, submarine cable, satellite earth station and space station applications, international broadcast stations, and other international items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cable landing license (CXT) $4,505; International Section 214 new authorization (DAG) $920; Space station geostationary application (BNY/BNZ) $4,175 per satellite; Non-geostationary systems CLW/CLY $17,670; Small satellites $2,555. Earth station application/renewal/assignment fees and many other international fees are listed across Tables 1–11. See §1.1107 Tables 1–11 for full detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of charges for Homeland services (CALEA petition fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments should be made electronically; manual filings/payments no longer accepted. Lists CALEA petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication Assistance for Law Enforcement (CALEA) Petitions (CLEA) fee amount $6,945.00. See §1.1109 and Commission website instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonrefundable nature of charges and limited refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: The charges required to accompany a request for the Commission's regulatory services listed in §§ 1.1102 through 1.1109 will not be refundable to the applicant irrespective of the Commission's disposition of that request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return or refund of charges will be made only in certain limited instances as set out at § 1.1115 of this subpart (§1.1110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment procedures and required fee form (FCC Form 159/159-E)
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedule of fees lists those applications and other filings that must be accompanied by an FCC Form 159, Remittance Advice, or the electronic version FCC Form 159-E, one of the forms automatically generated when an applicant accesses Commission on-line filing and payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may access online filing systems and fee payment module via provided URLs. Applications and filings not submitted in accordance with these instructions will be returned as unprocessable. Applications returned for additional info do not require an additional fee when resubmitted unless the info results in an increased fee. Original fee forfeited if corrections not resubmitted by deadline. If staff changes application status resulting in increased fee, applicant will be billed for the remainder under §1.1118(b). Note regarding tariff filings procedures may vary (§1.1111(a)-(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of payment: acceptable instruments and electronic payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual and multiple year regulatory fees must be paid electronically. Other fee payments may be in the form of a check, cashier's check, or money order drawn on a U.S. financial institution and payable to the FCC or by Visa, MasterCard, American Express, or Discover credit card. No other credit cards accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit card payments require completion of the credit card section of FCC Form 159. The Commission discourages cash. Personal or corporate checks dated more than six months or postdated checks not accepted; third party checks not accepted. Applicants are encouraged to submit payments electronically; specific electronic procedures announced in Bureau/Office fee filing guides; it is the payer's responsibility to ensure electronic payment is made as required. Wire transfer payments must follow instructions in the appropriate Bureau/Office fee filing guide. Applicants are required to submit one payment instrument and FCC Form 159 with each application; multiple payment instruments for a single application are not permitted (§1.1112(a)-(b)).
